name: Calf implants

lead: Calf implants are silicone prostheses placed under the fascia or muscle of the lower leg to add volume. People use them for thin calves that do not respond to training, for asymmetry or wasting, and bodybuilders seek them for size. The payoff is larger, more muscular-looking calves.

Implants were first reported in 1979. Surgeons have published single-center series and a 2019 review pooling 26 studies on 1,498 patients and 2,629 calves. Fat grafting and combined approaches are also described as alternatives. The evidence is surgeon-reported case series and reviews rather than controlled trials, and looksmaxxing forum discussion is limited.

paras: A surgeon makes an incision, typically behind the knee, and places a solid or gel-filled silicone implant beneath the fascia or in a plane between the calf muscles. The added volume shows after healing, with a period of restricted activity beforehand.

The 26-study review analysed complication rates by technique. Reported problems include seroma, implant displacement, capsular contracture, dissatisfaction leading to removal and, in one case, acute compartment syndrome with muscle necrosis. Regulation of implants and surgeons varies by country.

angle.text: A silicone implant placed in the calf adds lower-leg volume for larger, more muscular-looking calves, visible after healing. Evidence comes from surgical case series and a 26-study review.

lead: Calf augmentation is a cosmetic and reconstructive surgery that adds volume to the lower leg, most often with silicone implants placed beneath the fascia or muscle, and sometimes with fat grafting. [1][2] Indications include thin legs, asymmetry, bodybuilders seeking more muscle size and deformity from injury or illness. [1][2]

Calf implants were first reported in 1979, and early designs included silicone-gel implants and firm silicone rubber ones, with placement below the deep fascia and, later, in the plane between gastrocnemius and soleus. [3] Surgeons have published single-center series and a 2019 review pooling 26 studies on 1,498 patients and 2,629 calves. [2]

Available evidence is limited to such series and reviews; no randomized trials were found. In looksmaxxing communities the procedure is a niche topic; the sources reviewed contain no substantial forum discussion.

paras: Implants are made of solid semisoft silicone, which can be carved to fit, or of a firm shell containing cohesive silicone. [4] A 2000 report favoured soft silicone implants as more natural-looking than hard ones, placed over the gastrocnemius or beneath the fascia through an incision at the popliteal crease. [5]

A submuscular approach, between the gastrocnemius and soleus, was developed because subfascial implants had visible capsular contracture problems and firm implants could be felt through the skin. [3] A 2009 anthropometric study classified calf defects into five types to guide implant type, size and plane. [6] Fat grafting for calf augmentation has been reported as an alternative to silicone implants, and combined composite augmentation in staged procedures has been described. [7][8]

No randomized trials were identified. Evidence consists of case series and reviews. A 2017 series covering 1991-2016 included 50 patients who had 60 calf corrections, 23 aesthetic and 21 reconstructive; the surgeon rated results excellent-to-good in 30 of 37 followed patients and patients rated results very good in 18, good in 10, acceptable in 7 and bad in 2. [1]

A 2000 series of 100 patients (200 implants) reported no infections, ruptures or hematomas, four seromas that resolved, and removal of four implants in two dissatisfied patients. [5] A 2005 report described 18 patients at a Stockholm clinic, and a 2017 study examined the safety and efficacy of subfascial augmentation. [4][9]
A 2019 review analysed complication rates for subfascial implants, submuscular implants and fat grafting across 26 studies from 1993 to 2018. [2]

In the 2017 series, one 28-year-old professional bodybuilder developed acute anterior compartment syndrome in one leg; the implants were removed after 16 hours but muscle ischaemia and necrosis followed, requiring several operations. [1] Other reported issues include seroma, implant displacement and capsular contracture. [5][3] Anatomical and physiological considerations, including some health conditions, are cited as relevant to safety in staged composite augmentation. [8]

timeline.event: First report of calf augmentation, per a later surgical review. [3]
Technique of placing implants under the investing crural fascia worked out. [1]
Submuscular placement between gastrocnemius and soleus reported in six patients. [3]
